reason: Ninurta is 'lord of the earth' and the divine ploughman; the long catalog of stones in Lugal-e assigns flint to the sickle and makes cultivation possible only after his victory.
The slayer of Anzû and Asag, bearer of the speaking mace Sharur, and the warrior the great gods dispatch when cosmic order is stolen.
The thunder-storm and the hurricane winds are his weapons; his mythology is rooted in the meteorological violence of the Mesopotamian plain.
In Lugal-e he names each defeated stone and assigns it to temple, forge, and tool — a charter myth for mineral extraction and craft.
